positions.title: Embedded Software Engineer
positions.description:
Flight safety systems embedded software engineer leading the development, integration, test, and certification of an autonomous flight safety system in accordance with both mission and FAA/range safety requirements. 

Software responsibilities included integration and development of COTS and custom software as well as FPGA firmware onto custom hardware. Development of the flight control computers interface to the flight safety system. Lead software design reviews (PDR/CDR,etc) for the flight safety system.

Streamlined hardware acceptance and qualification testing by assisting in building out new testbeds and test environment infrastructure. Wrote, reviewed, and proposed acceptance and qualification test plans for flight safety avionics components. Created a tool suite to automate the creation of qualification and acceptance test report summaries to save weeks of man hours per individual serial no, and expedited formal data reviews with regulators. 

Participated and executed qualification and acceptance testing utilizing tools such as vibe tables and thermal chambers.
positions.insights: Skills: Software Infrastructure · C++ · Engineering · Embedded Software · Avionics Hardware Qualification

positions.title: Senior Embedded Software Engineer
positions.description:
Leveraged the use of an ARINC-653 real-time operating system for the development of new and novel software for an air vehicle data computer.

Developed FACE aligned/conformant software (IOSS, PSSS, and PCS layers).

Served as the software liaison to the avionics systems and test organizations for debugging, root cause analysis, and to provide insight on the hardware/software capabilities and low-level design.

positions.title: Flight Controls Engineer
positions.description:
Worked as a flight control software engineer writing and performing hardware-in-the-loop high level tests, test cases, and test procedures in C# in Systems Integration Lab.

Lead and participated in code and test reviews per the DO-178C DAL-A software development process.

Identify and remedy issues in the redundancy management software requirements and system architecture.

positions.title: Facility Supervisor
positions.description: My role as a Texas A&M Rec Sports supervisor included supervising 6-10 other employees, managing all operational aspects of the 500,000 sqft Rec Center, and being the lead employee when full-time professional staff is unavailable. This involves completing daily facility reports, enforcing policy violations and resolving any issue that may arise, the responsibility of opening and closing the facility on a regular basis, performing evaluations of other employees, and providing remedial training to employees when necessary. This position is also tasked with being the face of Texas A&M University when providing tours to visiting public school students and prospective students whose individual groups range from 1-100+ people.

projects.title: Programming a CPU
projects.description: This project included programming a CPU emulator in Verilog. Each individual component of a CPU was designed and implemented into a final functioning unit that would read in a set of instructions using the ARMv8 format and perform the desired task. It was also able to handle hazards through forwarding and pipeline stalls.

projects.title: Three Stage Transistor Amplifier
projects.description:
This project tested mine and a partner's knowledge of transistors and general analog circuits. It involved creating an amplifier that met certain specifications using only discrete components and MOSFET transistors. These specifications limited the input and output impedances, had a specific small signal voltage gain, a certain output voltage swing was required, and the low and high frequency poles had to be within a certain range. The designed circuit was simulated the circuit in MULTISIM and then implemented and tested physically in lab.

A report was then written that outlined each step taken during the design process and explained the reasoning behind it. It also included the detailed results and measurements taken in the simulation and during the physical demonstration of it.

It provided a great insight into the real world design process of analog amplifier circuits, using teamwork to accomplish a task, and how to write a detailed technical report over the design process.
